extension.summary: A green-phosphor radar scope showing the aircraft flying over you right now
extension.description: The Vintage Radar app's scope on your idle TV: a green (or amber, ice-blue or white) phosphor disc with range rings, a compass rose, a glowing sweep and aircraft blips that glide between updates and keep three sweep echoes. It shows the aircraft actually overhead, live from adsb.lol with OpenSky as a fallback, centred on the place and range you choose. The right side carries a nearest-first contact list and a spotlight card that rotates through every contact showing what the transponder reports: callsign, registration, type, squawk, category, altitude, speeds, headings, vertical rates, navigation settings, position, signal quality and the fix source. Four phosphors, CRT scanlines and vignette, dimming, full-screen or panel layout, and display detail for slow boxes. Any key or click exits. The companion app, Vintage Radar, is the same scope in a driveable window where clicking a contact opens its full card and you can find your location by name.
extension.disclaimer: Aircraft data comes from the volunteer-run adsb.lol and OpenSky Network APIs and is used as-is; it is not for navigation or flight safety. The typeface is Doto (SIL Open Font License 1.1), baked into texture atlases in the Vintage Radar library add-on.
